title: Add offline bundle inspection CLI for Support/SE (manifest + signature + hashes report)
creator: Dylan Brooks
description:
Problem
Support/SE teams troubleshooting air-gapped installs need a deterministic, copy/paste-friendly way to answer:
- What is in this offline bundle (versions/build id)?
- Is the manifest present and canonical (expected schema version)?
- Does the signature verify against the installer trust store? Which key?
- Do artifact hashes match what the manifest declares (to detect transfer corruption/tampering)?
- If verification fails, what exactly failed and what are the remediation steps?

Today this requires multiple manual steps (tar listing, manual openssl/cosign checks, eyeballing file hashes). This is slow, inconsistent, and error-prone during support escalations.

Goal
Add a CLI command to redwood-private-installer that can run fully offline and generates a concise, standardized report for support cases.

Non-goals (Phase 1)
- Not a replacement for full installer preflight; this is a diagnostic tool.
- Not a customer-managed signing flow (customer-signed bundles) beyond reporting what is present.
- Not a full SBOM viewer; only validate presence + hash/pointer.

Proposed UX
New command family:
- redwood-private-installer bundle inspect --bundle <path>
Optional flags:
- --verify            (verify signature and validate hashes referenced in manifest)
- --output text|json  (default: text)
- --report <path>     (write report to file; always prints a short summary to stdout)
- --trust-store <path> (optional override for support scenarios; default uses installer trust store)
- --time <rfc3339>    (diagnostic override for time-skew; does NOT change install behavior; report must clearly mark override)
- --no-hash-check     (skip hashing large artifacts; still checks manifest + signature)

Text output should be designed for ticket copy/paste (Jira/Slack) and include:
- Bundle path, detected bundle format version, manifest schema version
- Manifest digest (sha256 of canonical bytes) and signature file name (detached)
- Signature verification: PASS/FAIL + reason
- Trusted key id (kid/fingerprint) used, and which trust root entry matched
- Build identifiers: bundle build_id, product version, installer min_version
- Artifact summary counts: charts/images/model/runtime artifacts
- Hash validation summary: N checked, N ok, N mismatched, first 3 mismatches
- SBOM pointer + hash check result (if present)
- Downgrade metadata (if present): bundle version + channel + monotonic constraints

JSON output should be stable for tooling (Support automation) but we will keep it minimal in v1. JSON must not include secrets (no absolute host paths beyond provided bundle path; no environment dumps).

Implementation notes
- Reuse the same verification primitives as preflight (avoid drift): manifest canonicalization, signature envelope parsing, trust store matching, hash validation.
- Ensure command never attempts to fetch missing artifacts (air-gapped safe). If required artifact file is missing, report as FAIL with remediation.
- Performance: hashing can be expensive (multi-GB bundles). Default behavior:
  - If --verify is set, hash-check only manifest-referenced files under a size threshold (e.g., 2GB) and always hash the manifest + sig.
  - Provide --no-hash-check and print a warning that integrity checks are partial.
- Redaction: do not print file contents, tokens, registry creds, or K8s cluster state.

Acceptance criteria
- A support engineer can run a single command on a customer jump host and attach the output to a ticket.
- For a valid signed bundle, the tool reports PASS and identifies the signing key fingerprint.
- For common failure modes, output is actionable and consistent with installer preflight error taxonomy:
  - manifest missing
  - signature missing
  - signature invalid
  - unknown/untrusted key
  - hash mismatch (transfer corruption)
  - time validity issue (not-yet-valid/expired) with guidance
- Unit tests for report generation + parsing and at least one integration test with:
  - valid bundle
  - tampered manifest
  - swapped artifact
- Docs snippet added to internal Support/SE playbook and linked from verification failure runbook.

References
- Related GitHub PR (implementation): sources/github/redwood-private-installer/pr-24888-add-offline-bundle-inspect-command.json
- Follow-on: include inspect output in support bundle generation (ENG-4823/PR-25011)
- Support pain: SUP-31844, SUP-31892
comments: 2025-11-21 (Dev Patel): Strong +1. For pilots, we need a single pasteable block that includes key fingerprint, manifest digest, and the first mismatch path/hash if corruption is detected. This should reduce back-and-forth by days.

2025-12-02 (Marcus Lin): Please ensure inspect uses the same canonicalization code as signing/verification and that JSON output doesn’t inadvertently include sensitive host details. Also, time override must be explicitly labeled as diagnostic-only to avoid customers relying on it.

2025-12-08 (Owen Phillips): Can we include a short ‘Suggested next steps’ section when FAIL occurs? Example: for hash mismatch, recommend re-transfer using binary-safe tooling and verify checksums pre/post unzip.

2026-01-10 (Connor O'Brien): Prefer that inspect prints the bundle build_id and signing key kid in a single-line summary for quick grep across logs. Also add --output json for ingestion into Support automation later.

2026-01-22 (Devon Price): Landed PR-24888. Inspect command shares verifier library with preflight; added text + json output. Added size cap for hashing with explicit warning + --no-hash-check. Included time override with loud banner in report.
updates: 2025-12-05: Design drafted: output fields, error mapping, and flags. Sync with Support (Dev Patel) on pasteable format and minimal required fields.
2025-12-19: Implemented initial command skeleton and wired manifest reader + trust store loader. Pending: hash scan + integration tests.
2026-01-08: Added signature verification + key fingerprint reporting. Added basic JSON output; waiting on Security review for redaction.
2026-01-17: Added hash verification with threshold + --no-hash-check. Added failure remediation hints for top 5 errors.
2026-01-23: Merged. Docs snippet sent to DevEx for inclusion in internal air-gapped install guide; follow-up to include output in support bundle tracked separately.
